parsed.explanation: Combined national-state regime imposes tier-1 universal exposures: birth-sex facilities exclusion in state facilities, birth-sex passport/document regime with entry discrepancy leading to refusal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility, and birth-sex custody/hospital placement if detained or hospitalised. Documented immigration-custody forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse and prison conversion practices show severe post-outing harm, while a bathroom trespass arrest shows criminalisation is operative, not merely paper. No execution or routine presentation arrests are documented, national employment and hate-crime law, litigation and some enjoinments provide partial recourse, and many protections/enforcements vary by state and court outcome. For a travelling minor, state care ban, school pronoun/disclosure law and national orders targeting social transition add exposure. Above 0.25 organised targeting, below 0.55 administrative-only friction.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex passport policy, no new X markers, birth-sex documents; entry cable directs refusal on discrepancy/doubt and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation; passports reportedly confiscated/blocked.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; ACLU litigation pending; some executive orders enjoined; written fraud elements and limited waivers required, not automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from secondary screening to refusal, detention or fraud finding, then to birth-sex custody/facilities.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Bathroom trespass arrest with 24h in men's ward documented nationally; national prison conversion practices including hair cutting and hormone removal; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to depart; pretrial release, courts and counsel in principle; national hate-crime statute since 2009.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Detention for facilities/document offences exposes visitor to birth-sex placement and reported custodial abuse with limited consular/remedy speed.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: April 2023 state law allows restriction of bathroom use in many state-run facilities; national/state bans cover all/some government buildings in many states, 4 states criminalise in circumstances; state rated among worst for anti-trans legislation.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states plus capital district have no mapped ban, but this state does; some private settings not covered; exemptions for emergencies, chaperoning, out-of-order facilities in example statute.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal binary definition reinforces state facility bans; arrest risk follows use of congruent facilities in government buildings, schools, clinics.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors illegal in state since 2023 and 27 states; national orders target minor care, schools/teachers facilitating social transition, funding; hospital ward placement by document sex can out visitor.
care_services.protection: Adult care not documented as banned in dossier; emergency exemptions in facilities statute; some national orders blocked/enjoined.
care_services.interaction: Adult with minor: care denial, school disclosure/pronoun rules and teacher-prosecution orders interact with facilities and document exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders define sex as binary at birth, ban trans athletes and gender-identity facilities use, remove gender-ideology materials; counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; diversity of official hostility documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Counterterrorism text states powers not for mere disagreement; several orders enjoined; courts are actively litigating.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing enables facility, sports, school and entry enforcement and raises police/officer discretion at checkpoints.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans assigned-male-at-birth students from female sports, bans minor care, requires parental disclosure of trans students and permits pronoun/accommodation penalties; national orders direct investigation/prosecution of teachers using preferred names/pronouns.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented. No visitor-specific minor protection documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling minor in school/clinic settings faces disclosure, sports/facilities exclusion and care denial; guardian may face investigation exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Airport screening described as invasive and outing; no dated state incident of anti-trans violence documented; national public opinion 66% supports birth-sex documents, party platform linked trans people to predation though governor opposed it.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime prosecution available since 2009; one city municipal/rental protection from 2013; 78% in 2022 poll supported anti-discrimination law covering gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State hate-crime law excludes gender identity, so local police response may depend on national prosecution; screening can out visitor before street encounter.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and challenges to executive orders unresolved; Supreme Court allowed passport restrictions to take effect Nov 2025; corrections bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers from 2025; relationship of 2008/2023 birth-certificate rules unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, legal-aid FAQ, injunctions on some orders, national employment ruling 2020, city protections in one city.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow, partial and state-dependent; uncertainty itself affects travel timing but does not erase operative bans.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal state exposure and ineffective remedy for outed visitors, but here detention is less routine than systematic stops/fines, no unofficial file/extortion pattern, and courts/enjoinments are more active, so slightly above 0.35.

Closest: routine document/facilities exposure, detention and humiliation documented, imprisonment uncommon except fraud/trespass, slow legal aid. Custody abuse reports and minor-care bans make this case at the lower end of 0.45 tier.

Higher than 0.65 because national equality protection, apology/compensation and reliable release do not operate here; instead federal/state rules affirmatively require birth-sex documents/facilities and allow refusal/permanent ineligibility.

parsed.synthesis: Interaction is cumulative: home/foreign document mismatch triggers entry screening and possible refusal/fraud inquiry; inside the state, same mismatch drives facilities exclusion, hospital or custody placement by birth sex, and for minors school disclosure and care bans. Functioning courts and national employment/hate-crime law provide some recourse and prevent a 0.25 rating, but they do not override operative federal entry, facility and custody rules, especially where enforcement is efficient. No capital or routine sweep regime is documented, so risk is high-elevated rather than severe.
